You used plans, arrangements, schedules, actions in progress, routines, and stative verbs to build the complete robot.

GRAMMAR SCANNER

BE GOING TO

Use it for plans and intentions, and for predictions with evidence now.

We are going to build a robot.
Look at the smoke! It is going to stop.

PRESENT CONTINUOUS

Use it for actions happening now and for fixed future arrangements.

The robot is charging now.
I am meeting Leo at 4:30 tomorrow.

PRESENT SIMPLE

Use it for habits, routines, facts, and official timetables.

Maya repairs robots on Fridays.
The train leaves at 8:10.

STATIVE VERBS

Verbs such as know, believe, like, want, need, understand, belong and remember are usually not continuous.

I know the answer. ✓
I am knowing the answer. ✗

SAME VERB, DIFFERENT MEANING

Some verbs can be stative or active. “Think” can mean “believe” or “consider”. “Have” can mean “own” or “experience”.

I think this is safe. / I am thinking about a new design.
I have a sensor. / We are having lunch.

FAST CLUE SCANNER

now / right now → often Present Continuous
every day / usually → often Present Simple
timetable / program → Present Simple
decided / plan → going to
agreed / arranged → Present Continuous
